chunks.section: Undergraduate Academic Regulations (2023 Edition - Superseded Policy)
chunks.text: Undergraduate Academic Regulations (2023 Edition - Superseded Policy): *Notice: This edition is superseded by the 2026 Regulations and is maintained for historical archival and rollback verification.*

chunks.title: FAST-NUCES Undergraduate Academic Rules (2023 Edition)
chunks.text:
1. Attendance Regulations (Historical 2023): 1.1 Under the 2023 academic rules, a student must attend at least 75 percent of scheduled class lectures and lab sessions to sit for the final exam. (Note: the 2026 edition raised this threshold to 80 percent).
1.2 A student falling below the 75 percent requirement received

chunks.title: FAST-NUCES Undergraduate Academic Rules (2023 Edition)
chunks.text:
to 80 percent).
1.2 A student falling below the 75 percent requirement received the grade FA.

chunks.title: FAST-NUCES Undergraduate Academic Rules (2023 Edition)
chunks.text:
2. Academic Warning & Probation (Historical 2023): 2.1 A student whose CGPA dropped below 1.75 was placed on Academic Warning at the end of a regular semester.
2.2 A student remaining on warning for two consecutive semesters was dismissed from the university (academic drop).

chunks.title: FAST-NUCES Undergraduate Academic Rules (2023 Edition)
chunks.text:
3. Course Repetition Policy (Historical 2023): 3.1 A student was eligible to repeat any course in which their earned grade was C or lower.
3.2 In the 2023 policy, when a course was repeated to improve CGPA, the maximum permissible grade on the repeated attempt was capped at B (3.00 grade points).

chunks.title: FAST-NUCES Undergraduate Academic Rules (2026 Edition)
chunks.text:
1. General Degree Requirements & Timeline: 1.1 The minimum duration to complete a four-year Bachelor of Science (BS) degree programme in Software Engineering, Computer Science, or Data Science is four (4) academic years (8 regular semesters).
1.2 The maximum allowable duration to complete an undergraduate Bachelor's de

chunks.title: FAST-NUCES Undergraduate Academic Rules (2026 Edition)

chunks.text:
atically struck off university rolls.
1.3 Degree award requires earning at least 130 credit hours, satisfying core, elective, and university distribution requirements, and attaining a minimum final Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA) of 2.00 on a 4.00 scale.

chunks.title: FAST-NUCES Undergraduate Academic Rules (2026 Edition)
chunks.text:
2. Attendance Policy & Condonation: 2.1 Attendance in lectures, tutorial sessions, and laboratory classes is mandatory. A student must maintain an attendance percentage of at least 80 percent in each registered course to be eligible to appear in the final examination.
2.2 If a student's attendance falls below 80 percen

chunks.title: FAST-NUCES Undergraduate Academic Rules (2026 Edition)
chunks.text:
ar in the final examination.
2.2 If a student's attendance falls below 80 percent in any course, the instructor shall assign the failing grade "FA" (Failure due to Attendance). An FA grade contributes zero grade points per credit hour and directly reduces both SGPA and CGPA.
2.3 The Head of Department (HOD) in consulta

chunks.title: FAST-NUCES Undergraduate Academic Rules (2026 Edition)
chunks.text:
irectly reduces both SGPA and CGPA.
2.3 The Head of Department (HOD) in consultation with the Academic Director may condone up to a maximum of 5 percent absence strictly for verified, documented medical emergencies or official university representation. Under no circumstances may attendance below 75 percent be condoned

chunks.title: FAST-NUCES Undergraduate Academic Rules (2026 Edition)
chunks.text: presentation. Under no circumstances may attendance below 75 percent be condoned.

chunks.title: FAST-NUCES Undergraduate Academic Rules (2026 Edition)
chunks.text:
3. Semester Load & Course Registration: 3.1 The standard semester course load for regular undergraduate students in good standing is five (5) courses or between 15 to 18 credit hours.
3.2 Students maintaining a CGPA of 3.00 or higher may be permitted by the Academic Advisor to register for an additional course up to a

chunks.title: FAST-NUCES Undergraduate Academic Rules (2026 Edition)
chunks.text:
permitted by the Academic Advisor to register for an additional course up to a maximum overload limit of 21 credit hours in a regular semester.
3.3 Students with active academic warnings or probationary status are restricted to a maximum course load of 12 credit hours (typically 3 or 4 courses) to facilitate academic

chunks.title: FAST-NUCES Undergraduate Academic Rules (2026 Edition)
chunks.text: ourse load of 12 credit hours (typically 3 or 4 courses) to facilitate academic recovery.

chunks.title: FAST-NUCES Undergraduate Academic Rules (2026 Edition)
chunks.text:
4. Academic Warning, Probation, and Dismissal: 4.1 Academic standing is computed at the conclusion of every Fall and Spring regular semester.
4.2 A student whose cumulative grade point average (CGPA) falls below 2.00 at the end of a regular semester is placed on Academic Warning.
4.3 A student who remains on Academic W

chunks.title: FAST-NUCES Undergraduate Academic Rules (2026 Edition)
chunks.text:
semester is placed on Academic Warning.
4.3 A student who remains on Academic Warning for two consecutive semesters is placed on Academic Probation.
4.4 A student who remains on Academic Warning or Probation for three (3) consecutive semesters without raising their CGPA to 2.00 or above is dropped from the degree prog

chunks.title: FAST-NUCES Undergraduate Academic Rules (2026 Edition)
chunks.text: ters without raising their CGPA to 2.00 or above is dropped from the degree programme (academic dismissal).

chunks.title: FAST-NUCES Undergraduate Academic Rules (2026 Edition)
chunks.text:
5. Course Repetition & Prerequisite Failures: 5.1 A student may repeat any course in which an earned grade is below C (including grades C-, D+, D, and F) to improve their CGPA.
5.2 Under the current 2026 policy, when a student repeats a course, only the grade of the most recent attempt counts toward CGPA calculation, e

chunks.title: FAST-NUCES Undergraduate Academic Rules (2026 Edition)
chunks.text:
rse, only the grade of the most recent attempt counts toward CGPA calculation, even if the repeated attempt resulted in a lower grade. All prior attempts remain visible on the official transcript annotated as repeated.
5.3 If a student fails a prerequisite course (grade F), they are strictly prohibited from registering

chunks.title: FAST-NUCES Undergraduate Academic Rules (2026 Edition)
chunks.text: s a prerequisite course (grade F), they are strictly prohibited from registering for the subsequent advanced course until the prerequisite has been repeated and cleared with a minimum passing grade of D.

chunks.section: 3. Fee Refund Schedule upon Course or Programme Withdrawal
chunks.text:
3. Fee Refund Schedule upon Course or Programme Withdrawal: 3.1 If a student formally drops a course or withdraws from the semester within the first ten (10) calendar days of the start of classes: 100 percent of tuition fees refunded.
3.2 If withdrawal occurs between day 11 and day 20 of the semester: 50 percent of tui

chunks.text:
f withdrawal occurs between day 11 and day 20 of the semester: 50 percent of tuition fees refunded.
3.3 After day 20 of classes: Zero (0) percent refund; the student forfeits all tuition fees for that semester. Admission fee is strictly non-refundable under all circumstances.

2. Grading Scheme and SGPA / CGPA Calculation: 2.1 Grade points are awarded on a four-point scale: A (4.00), A- (3.67), B+ (3.33), B (3.00), B- (2.67), C+ (2.33), C (2.00), C- (1.67), D+ (1.33), D (1.00), F (0.00).
2.2 The Semester Grade Point Average (SGPA) is computed as the sum of products of credit hours and grade

int Average (SGPA) is computed as the sum of products of credit hours and grade points divided by the total credit hours registered in the semester:
    SGPA = Sum(Credit_Hours * Grade_Points) / Sum(Credit_Hours).
2.3 The Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA) represents the weighted average of grade points earned in al

chunks.title: FAST-NUCES Student Code of Conduct & Disciplinary Policy
chunks.text:
1. Code of Academic Integrity & Plagiarism: 1.1 All students are expected to adhere strictly to the highest standards of academic honesty in all examinations, laboratory projects, assignments, and semester research papers.
1.2 Plagiarism is defined as the intentional or unintentional presentation of another individual'

chunks.title: FAST-NUCES Student Code of Conduct & Disciplinary Policy
chunks.text:
defined as the intentional or unintentional presentation of another individual's work, code, concepts, or textual phrasing as one's own without appropriate citation and attribution.
1.3 In Software Development and Computer Science courses, source code copying from peers, public repositories, or generative models witho

chunks.title: FAST-NUCES Student Code of Conduct & Disciplinary Policy
chunks.text: source code copying from peers, public repositories, or generative models without authorization constitutes serious academic dishonesty.

chunks.title: FAST-NUCES Student Code of Conduct & Disciplinary Policy
chunks.text:
2. Disciplinary Actions & Penalties: 2.1 When an instructor or university integrity committee confirms an infraction of academic dishonesty or plagiarism:
   - First minor offense: The student receives an immediate failing grade "F" in the respective assignment or course, accompanied by an official written reprimand pl

chunks.title: FAST-NUCES Student Code of Conduct & Disciplinary Policy
chunks.text:
respective assignment or course, accompanied by an official written reprimand placed in the permanent record.
   - Second or severe offense: The Academic Disciplinary Committee shall suspend the student's registration for one or two regular semesters.
   - Third offense: Permanent expulsion from FAST-NUCES across all c

chunks.title: FAST-NUCES Student Code of Conduct & Disciplinary Policy
chunks.text:
semesters.
   - Third offense: Permanent expulsion from FAST-NUCES across all campuses without possibility of re-admission.
2.2 When a student's registration is suspended, they are barred from attending classes, entering university premises, utilizing laboratory workstations, or participating in campus extracurricular

chunks.title: FAST-NUCES Student Code of Conduct & Disciplinary Policy
chunks.text: s, utilizing laboratory workstations, or participating in campus extracurricular activities for the duration of the suspension.

chunks.section: 3. Campus Conduct, Dress Code, and Property
chunks.text:
3. Campus Conduct, Dress Code, and Property: 3.1 Smoking, vaping, and possession of illicit substances anywhere on campus premises, including cafeterias and parking lots, is strictly prohibited and subject to immediate fine and disciplinary review.
3.2 Willful destruction, tampering, or unauthorized reconfiguration of
